text: I'll start with the paged workload.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The inventory-sync worker runs as ServiceAccount inventory/inventory-sync and reads its feed configuration from the Kubernetes API (ConfigMap inventory/inventory-sources). The only RoleBinding in the namespace, RoleBinding inventory/inventory-reader-binding, grants Role inventory/inventory-reader (get and list on configmaps) to a subject named "inventory-synk", which is not a ServiceAccount that exists in the namespace — the accounts that exist are default and inventory-sync. Because of that one-character subject name typo, the worker's identity holds no permissions, its API fetch is rejected with HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden, and the pod falls back to "serving stale inventory snapshot" while staying Running and Ready — so the storefront keeps showing counts that never refresh.
arguments.mechanism: RoleBinding inventory/inventory-reader-binding has .subjects[0].name set to "inventory-synk" instead of the ServiceAccount that actually exists and that Deployment inventory/inventory-sync runs as, "inventory-sync", so Role inventory/inventory-reader (get and list on configmaps) is bound to nobody. The worker's read of its feed configuration is rejected — "sync fetch error: wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden" — and it falls back to "serving stale inventory snapshot" instead of fetching fresh counts.

ruled_out.ruling_claim: The ServiceAccount named by the Deployment does exist in the namespace, so identity is not missing.
ruled_out.quote: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync

verification.command: kubectl -n inventory get rolebinding inventory-reader-binding -o yaml

arguments.root_cause_statement: The inventory-sync worker runs as ServiceAccount inventory/inventory-sync and reads its feed configuration from the Kubernetes API. The only RoleBinding in the namespace, RoleBinding inventory/inventory-reader-binding, grants Role inventory/inventory-reader (get and list on configmaps) to a subject named "inventory-synk", which is not a ServiceAccount that exists in the namespace — the accounts that exist are default and inventory-sync. Because of that one-character subject name typo the worker's identity holds no permissions, its API fetch is rejected with HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden, and the pod falls back to serving a stale inventory snapshot while staying Running and Ready, so the storefront counts never refresh.
arguments.mechanism: RoleBinding inventory/inventory-reader-binding has .subjects[0].name set to "inventory-synk" instead of "inventory-sync", the ServiceAccount that actually exists and that the paged worker runs as, so Role inventory/inventory-reader (get and list on configmaps) is bound to no existing identity. The worker's read of its feed configuration is therefore rejected — "sync fetch error: wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden" — and it falls back to "serving stale inventory snapshot" instead of fetching fresh counts.

evidence.claim: The paged worker pod is Running and Ready with no restarts, so the staleness is not a crash.
evidence.quote: pod/inventory-sync-5cf949f7f9-czxsq phase=Running labels={app=inventory-sync, pod-template-hash=5cf949f7f9} node=incident-lab-control-plane sync(ready=True,restarts=0)

evidence.claim: The worker's own logs show its fetch is rejected with 403.
evidence.quote: sync fetch error: wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

evidence.claim: After the 403 the worker explicitly serves stale data, matching the data-freshness alert.
The Deployment runs the pod as ServiceAccount inventory-sync.
The only RoleBinding names a subject that does not match the running ServiceAccount.
The RoleBinding spec itself carries the misspelled ServiceAccount subject.
The Role that would have granted the needed read access covers configmaps with get and list.

ruled_out.alternative: The ServiceAccount named by the Deployment does not exist, so the pod has no identity at all.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The ServiceAccount inventory-sync does exist in the namespace; only the binding's subject name is wrong.
ruled_out.quote: serviceaccounts that exist in inventory: default, inventory-sync

ruled_out.alternative: The Role grants the wrong resources or verbs, so even a correct binding would not help.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Role inventory-reader already grants get and list on configmaps, which is what the worker needs to read its feed configuration.

ruled_out.alternative: A missing or misnamed ConfigMap reference in the pod template breaks the sync.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both ConfigMaps the workload depends on exist with the expected keys, so the failure is not an unresolved config reference.

verification.command: kubectl -n inventory get rolebinding inventory-reader-binding -o yaml
